title: 2024 AMC 10A Problem 22
statement: Let \(\mathcal{K}\) be the kite formed by joining two right triangles with legs \(1\) and \(\sqrt3\) along a common hypotenuse. Eight copies of \(\mathcal{K}\) are used to form the polygon shown below. What is the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

solutions.text: Each half of a kite is a \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangle, so its edges have the shown lengths and directions. Take \(A=(0,0)\) and \(AB\) horizontal. The horizontal span in the figure is six unit lengths, so \(B=(6,0).\) Along the outer boundary from \(A\) to \(C,\) the three edges have vectors \(\sqrt3(\cos30^\circ,\sin30^\circ),\) \(\sqrt3(\cos90^\circ,\sin90^\circ),\) and \((1,0).\) Their sum is \((\tfrac52,\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}),\) so \(C=(\tfrac52,\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}).\) Thus \(AB=6\) and the altitude from \(C\) is \(\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{2},\) giving area \(\tfrac12\cdot6\cdot\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}=\tfrac{9\sqrt3}{2}.\) Therefore, the answer is B.
hints: Each kite is two \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangles (legs \(1\) and \(\sqrt3,\) hypotenuse \(2\)); set up coordinates from these lengths
Take \(A=(0,0)\) and \(AB\) horizontal; \(AB\) is six unit lengths, while the boundary from \(A\) to \(C\) uses lengths \(\sqrt3,\sqrt3,1\) at angles \(30^\circ,90^\circ,0^\circ\)
